descricao_original: A second category of Schwann cells surrounds axons in peripheral nerves and consists of non-myelinating and myelinating types. Non-myelinating Schwann cells invest numerous small axons, with each axon aligning in a groove on the cell. Myelinating Schwann cells ensheath single axons with numerous spiraling wraps of membrane, forming a myelin segment or internode. A series of myelinating Schwann cells forms a segmented myelin sheath along a single axon. The myelin sheath is a lipid-rich, insulating wrapping of an axon, which increases the conduction velocity of an action potential. 1000x
